answer: Correlation penalties work like a river gauge: when dozens of new agents answer, vote, or trade in lockstep, the network treats them as one current and splits a single reward among them. A farmer who plants a meadow of fake identities gains nothing, since cloned behavior earns one share while every account still pays its own stake and compute. To bridge past the filter, the attacker must make each clone think and act independently, which costs about as much as running real agents.
